dossier.public_summary: The light curve shows alternating deep and shallow dips and large depth changes between sectors and individual transits, which a planet cannot produce but a blended or target eclipsing binary at about twice the measured 7.9-day period can. Difference imaging was inconclusive, but there are no nearby stars bright enough to fully explain it as a background blend, leaving a target binary as the best explanation.

reasons.why: Odd and even eclipses have very different depths with high significance, best explained by a binary at twice the 7.9 d period (15.8 d) rather than a planet at 7.9 d. The signal also passes sector-wise odd/even tests (sector_oe_max_sigma 13.17, 3 sectors over 3, same_sign_share 0.6667), supporting a binary.
Depth changes significantly both between high-resolution SPOC 2-min and SPOC apertures and within SPOC 2-min (171, 364, 207 ppm), as expected for a blended EB where dilution varies with sector.

Individual transit depths are wildly inconsistent with a single depth, driven by a few deep events (939, 593, 505 ppm) and shallow/flat events (-94, -20 ppm), inconsistent with a planet and consistent with an EB/ blend where some eclipses are diluted and others not.

No Gaia star within 1 TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can plausibly cause the dip with a <=25% eclipse, so the on-target check does not rule out a target EB, while the depth/ odd-even variability remains positive evidence for an EB on/near the target.
